title: The Signal That Shouldn’t Exist
narration: A single pulse—52 times a second—echoes through the Pacific. No blue whale sings this high. No fin whale this loud. [gasp] What creature makes this sound?
visual_goal: Underwater hydrophone feed: a waveform spikes at 52Hz, alien against the ocean’s static. Cut to a lone whale surfacing, its call visualized as a glowing pulse.

title: First Heard in the Cold War
narration: 1989. The U.S. Navy’s SOSUS array—built to track submarines—picks up a call. Not Russian. Not whale. Something… else.
visual_goal: Grainy 1980s sonar screen flickers with the 52Hz signal. Cut to a submarine silhouette dissolving into ocean waves.

title: The Whale That Doesn’t Belong
narration: Blue whales hum at 10-40Hz. Fin whales at 20Hz. This one? 52Hz. Too high. Too loud. Like a violin in a drumline.
visual_goal: Split-screen: left, a blue whale’s deep rumble; right, the 52Hz whale’s sharp pulse. Overlay decibel meters—160dB vs 140dB.

sfx_events.at: Like a violin in a drumline

title: A Decade of Silence
narration: For years, it sang alone. No answers. No matches. Just… 52Hz, year after year.
visual_goal: Time-lapse of ocean waves with the 52Hz waveform pulsing steadily across the screen. Text: “1990… 1991… 1992…”

title: The Migration Map
narration: 100,000 kilometers tracked. From California to Alaska. Always alone. Always 52Hz.
visual_goal: Animated map: a glowing path traces the whale’s route across the Pacific. Dots mark hydrophone detections.

title: Why No Answers?
narration: No breaching. No calves. No social calls. Just… this. Why hasn’t it found its kind?
visual_goal: Underwater footage of the whale swimming in empty ocean. Text overlay: “No observed breeding. No interactions.”

title: The Hybrid Theory
narration: Genetic tests? Inconclusive. Acoustic clues? Suggest blue-fin mix. A whale out of time.
visual_goal: Microscopic view of whale tissue next to blue/fin whale DNA strands. The 52Hz waveform overlays as a shadow.

title: Winter’s Song
narration: Peak activity in winter. When the ocean is loudest. When the whale’s call cuts through the noise.
visual_goal: Stormy Pacific waves with the 52Hz pulse cutting through static. Text: “Winter 2023: 160dB detected.”

title: The Longest Record
narration: 30 years. Over 30 years of this single note. The longest acoustic record of any marine mammal.
visual_goal: Timeline: 1989 to 2024. The 52Hz waveform pulses steadily, growing into a dense graph.

title: The Whale That Remains
narration: A voice in the dark. A mystery unsolved. The loneliest song in the ocean. [whisper] Listen.
visual_goal: Final shot: the whale dives into abyssal blue. The 52Hz pulse fades into static. Text: “Still singing.”
